services.description: Agents run here, and the app hears what they do.
Sound for plugins, played by the tab that runs the plugin workers.
How agents and plugins talk to each other and to the person, by message rather than by calling each other.
Things a person (or an agent) can do in an app, named once by the plugin that does them, and run from anywhere: a command palette, a keyboard shortcut, or a model's tool call.
Tools for looking inside a running kernel, which no app needs to run.
Mail a server plugin sends, with the `email` permission.
A folder of files the person works on, such as a Hugo site: on their disk, if they pick one, or a private folder in the browser until they do.
A game loop, with every rule of the game in plugins.
Undo and redo for the person, across every write to an app's collections, whichever plugin made it: a delete in a table, an edit in a form, a book a plugin imported, a change an agent made.
Files opened with an app.
One way for any plugin to ask a language model, whoever makes the model.
Apps a person makes in the browser, by describing them to the app maker (std/maker/app-maker.agent.md) or by hand.
The operating system's notifications, so a plugin can tell the person something while they are in another tab or app (the writer agent has finished, a long export is done).
Lets agents that live outside the app (a browser's own assistant, Claude Code, any MCP client) use it.
The app's own page, as far as a plugin's places reach into it.
The kernel describes what is running in it, for debuggers (demos/debugger/).
A screen for every address: the reading list opened at /demos/reading-list/book/42 shows the screen `/book/42`, so a person can bookmark or share it, and back and forward move between screens.
Work a plugin wants done later, once or again and again, with the `schedule` permission.

Sharing out, and sharing in: a plugin can hand a link or some text to the system's share sheet (Web Share), and an app installed from the browser can be a place to share to (a share target), so a page shared from the browser lands in the reading list.
What lets an app open in a space (/s/<space>/…) and be shared by its members.
The service methods a plugin may call, described as tools a language model can call.

Import and export for the person: a collection out to a CSV or JSON file they keep, open in a spreadsheet or take to another app, and a file they choose (a bank's statement, a list from a spreadsheet, an earlier export) into a collection.
